questions.question: Where should the overhead inside rearview mirror be positioned?

options.text: To see the rear tires.
To see all students on the bus.
To see the floor of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: To see all students on the bus.
questions.explanation: Position the overhead mirror to show the top of the rear window. This lets you see all students, including those sitting directly behind you.

questions.question: How should you do a conventional parallel parking maneuver?

options.text: Back up past the space, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
Pull forward directly into the space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space. Then back into it, getting the rear of your vehicle close to the back of the space. Your vehicle must fit completely within the space.

questions.question: If you need to exit the bus to check on a student, what should you do?

options.text: Leave the bus running.
Turn off the bus and take the key.
Ask a student to watch the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the bus and take the key.
questions.explanation: Secure the bus by turning it off and taking the key. Then check around and under the bus for the missing student.

questions.question: If a railroad gate does not go back up after a train passes, what should you do?

options.text: Drive around the gate.
Wait for another vehicle to cross first to see if it is safe.
Call your dispatcher.

questions.correctAnswerText: Call your dispatcher.
questions.explanation: Do not drive around the lowered gate. Call your dispatcher to report the problem.

questions.question: Why should a bus stop at least 10 feet away from waiting students?

options.text: Students will walk to the bus, so you can watch their movements.
Buses are difficult to drive.
Students may get scared of the approaching bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Students will walk to the bus, so you can watch their movements.
questions.explanation: Stopping 10 feet away makes students walk to the bus. This allows you to watch them carefully.

questions.question: What should you watch for as students exit the bus?

options.text: That they leave in pairs.
That they do not get caught on the handrail or door.
That they do not talk while exiting.

questions.correctAnswerText: That they do not get caught on the handrail or door.
questions.explanation: Students can be injured if their clothing, accessories, or bodies get caught on a handrail or door. Watch carefully as students exit to make sure they all unload safely.

questions.question: If your bus has a manual transmission, what should you never do when crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: Change gears.
Use the brakes.
Look both ways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change gears.
questions.explanation: Do not shift gears while crossing tracks. Your bus could stall and get stuck.

questions.question: When exiting a bus, you must:

options.text: Never touch the handrail.
Always hold the handrail.
Move quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always hold the handrail.
questions.explanation: Face the bus and maintain three points of contact at all times. Keep holding the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may cause you to fail the skills test.

questions.question: When should you adjust a bus's mirrors?

options.text: Before you start driving.
While you are driving.
At the first stoplight after starting your shift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Check and adjust mirrors before you start any trip.

questions.question: If students cause a disturbance while others are getting off the bus, what should you do?

options.text: Go to the back immediately to handle it while students unload.
Wait until all students have unloaded, then handle it.
Ask a student near the disturbance to handle it while you watch.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until all students have unloaded, then handle it.
questions.explanation: Focus completely on loading and unloading students. Wait until students have safely exited before you deal with any behavior problems on the bus.

questions.question: When students board a bus, where should they sit?

options.text: In the back row first.
In the back row only after all other seats are filled.
As far from the driver as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the back row only after all other seats are filled.
questions.explanation: Students should fill front seats first. Sitting closer to the front is safer in case of a rear-end collision. Students with special needs should sit near the driver.

questions.question: If your driving test route has no railroad crossing, what might happen?

options.text: You will not do anything about a crossing.
The examiner may ask you to explain how to cross railroad tracks.
You will have to take a different route.

questions.correctAnswerText: The examiner may ask you to explain how to cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: During your on-road driving test, the examiner may ask you to explain and show how to cross railroad tracks at a practice location if there is no real crossing on your route.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in high winds?

options.text: Loosen your grip on the steering wheel.
Speed up.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: A school bus can be pushed by strong winds. Hold the steering wheel firmly, watch for wind gusts, and drive slowly. Contact your dispatcher if needed.

questions.question: When getting out of a vehicle, a driver should:

options.text: Jump directly from the seat to the ground.
Keep at least one hand on the vehicle.
Face the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Face the vehicle.
questions.explanation: During the basic vehicle control skills test, you must face the vehicle and hold onto it with three points of contact at all times. For a bus, hold the handrail. Improper exit will cause automatic failure.

questions.question: A post-trip inspection should include everything except:

options.text: Looking for items left on the bus.
Checking for sleeping students.
Opening windows.

questions.correctAnswerText: Opening windows.
questions.explanation: After a trip ends, check for sleeping students, lost items, open windows or doors, mechanical problems, and damage.

questions.question: Why should you park at least 10 feet away from students when picking them up?

options.text: You can see their movements clearly.
It is hard to park any closer.
Students need the exercise.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see their movements clearly.
questions.explanation: Parking 10 feet away makes students walk to the bus. This lets you watch them and keep them safe.

questions.question: When students are boarding, the driver should do everything except:

options.text: Check mirrors for students running to the bus.
Count students and make sure all board.
Allow students to board in pairs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow students to board in pairs.
questions.explanation: Count waiting students and confirm they all board. Check mirrors for running students. Students must board one at a time in a single line.

questions.question: When approaching a bus stop, the driver should:

options.text: Honk the horn.
Drive slowly.
Talk to students on the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly.
questions.explanation: Always drive slowly and carefully when approaching a bus stop.

questions.question: Loading and unloading students from a bus:

options.text: Is safe and does not need supervision.
Is dangerous and needs supervision.
Can happen without the driver present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is dangerous and needs supervision.
questions.explanation: More students are hurt during loading and unloading than while riding. Drivers must always supervise and follow safety rules during these times.

questions.question: If you exit your vehicle incorrectly during the basic vehicle control skills test, what happens?

options.text: You fail only that exercise.
You lose extra points on your final score.
You automatically fail the entire test.

questions.correctAnswerText: You automatically fail the entire test.
questions.explanation: You must face the vehicle and hold it with three points of contact when exiting. For a bus, hold the handrail. Bad exit technique causes automatic failure.
